name: EHIVE stake top-up rewards accrued on the new amount
summary: EHIVE.stake() added a top-up to the existing stake before crediting earnings, so the reward for the whole period since the stake began was computed on the enlarged balance. The attacker opened zero-amount stakes from 28 contracts weeks earlier, then passed flash-bought EHIVE through them, each staking it and unstaking with the back-dated reward minted, and sold the inflated balance into the EHIVE/WETH pair.
notes: The minted EHIVE is unpriced, so it is valued at what its sale realised (rule 12): the EHIVE/WETH pair's net WETH outflow in the anchor, which also repaid the flash-bought EHIVE.

Earlier exploits: replaying every successful stake, claim and unstake call from deployment to the anchor, the excess the bug paid on all earlier top-ups totals 1.68B EHIVE (about 3 ETH at pool prices) spread over ordinary users; the largest single excess, 0.23B EHIVE in 0xf4e55c65 by long-time staker 0xe22e9db2 (whose large mints are returned principal), was worth about 0.38 ETH. No mint above 1B EHIVE followed the anchor before block 18300000.
